name: Bend
tax_rate: 10.4% city + 1.5% state (no county TLT inside city limits); FY2025-26 city collections $15,166,602
deadline_pattern: Bend Cultural Tourism Fund (BCTF) applications open early February and close late March (March 27, 2026 for FY2026-27); awards announced mid/late May; funds available July 1 for projects Sept 1 to June 30. Bend Sustainability Fund (capital projects) opens mid-November and closes mid-January (Jan 16, 2026), awards in March. 2027 BCTF dates not yet posted.
typical_open: Early February (BCTF marketing grants); mid-November (Bend Sustainability Fund)
annual_pool: BCTF: $300,000 per year (2025 and 2026 cycles), about 7.5% of Visit Bend's budget; Bend Sustainability Fund: about $500,000 per year for capital tourism facilities
contact: Laurel MacMillan, BCTF Grant Administrator, laurel@laurelmacmillan.com, 503-803-8260; Zavier Borja, Destination Stewardship Director, Visit Bend (Bend Sustainability Fund; contact via sustainability.visitbend.com)
notes: The City of Bend contracts its tourism share of room tax to Visit Bend, and Visit Bend runs two TLT-funded grant rounds: the Bend Cultural Tourism Fund ($300,000/yr for marketing of arts, culture and events that draw visitors from 50+ miles, with emphasis on shoulder season and winter; large grants max $40,000, small marketing/research grants max $10,000) and the Bend Sustainability Fund (about $500,000/yr for shovel-ready tourism facilities with a 10-year life). An independent 10-member BCTF Commission scores applications (80 of 100 points minimum) and recommends awards; the Visit Bend board has historically adopted recommendations in full. For-profits, nonprofits, government agencies and individuals may apply to BCTF; one application per year per organization. 2026 BCTF round drew nearly $950,000 in requests for $300,000. No statement located on HB 4148 (2027).
members_source: https://culture.visitbend.com/information-resources links a 'Current Commissioners' PDF (May 2024) that could not be retrieved; no names published in news coverage. Commission is 10 volunteer members serving two-year terms ending in December (max three terms); commissioners may not work for an applicant organization. Recruitment runs in March (https://ktvz.com/?p=1322513).

presentation.pattern: No applicant presentation described; a required pre-application eligibility review precedes the full application, and a panel of BCTF Commissioners and external panelists scores written applications

meeting_schedule: BCTF Commission meets as needed around the annual cycle; public meeting minutes 2021 to January 2025 are posted at culture.visitbend.com/information-resources. Visit Bend board meets monthly and approves awards at its May meeting.
pool_note: City of Bend collected $15,166,602 in room tax in FY2025-26; the tourism share goes to Visit Bend under contract. Dollars open to outside applicants are the BCTF ($300,000) plus the Bend Sustainability Fund (about $500,000), roughly $800,000 per year. The remainder funds Visit Bend operations and marketing and the city's general fund share.

name: Clackamas County
tax_rate: 6% county-wide + 1.5% state (cities may add their own)
deadline_pattern: Strategic Investment Program grants are decided by the Tourism Development Council each year; a roughly $500,000 slate was voted in February 2026 for the 2025-26 program and the program was raised to $600,000 in June 2026. Application window dates are not posted publicly; the county says to sign up for grant notifications. The separate one-time Tourism Business Grant Program ($1M) ran May 14 to June 18, 2026.
annual_pool: Strategic Investment Program about $500,000 (2025-26), increased to $600,000 (2026-27); plus one-time $1,000,000 Tourism Business Grant Program (2026, for-profit tourism businesses, two $500,000 tracks)
contact: Lizzie Keenan, Executive Director, Clackamas County Tourism (Oregon's Mt. Hood Territory); Samara Phelps, former Director of Tourism, 971-334-9479; Tourism Business Grant Program: Office of Economic Development, 4biz@clackamas.us, 503-742-4249
notes: The county's 6% room tax (after the County Fair allotment and a 2% finance fee) funds the Office of Tourism, which is guided by a nine-member Tourism Development Council (TDC) appointed by the county commissioners. The TDC runs an annual Strategic Investment Program (previously called Tourism Development Grants and the Community Partnership Program) that has awarded $1.335 million in recent years for tourism experience projects such as the Trillium Lake boardwalk, theater upgrades, trails, heritage sites and county parks; it also sponsors public events (for example accessibility glasses at the Swan Island Dahlia Festival and Wooden Shoe Tulip Festival). In 2026 the county added a one-time $1M Tourism Business Grant Program for for-profit tourism businesses run by Economic Development. The TDC chair submitted testimony opposing HB 4148 (Feb 2026), saying it would end destination development and partner support programs.

name: Rockaway Beach
deadline_pattern: Off-Season Tourism Marketing Grant and Facade Improvement Grant open March 1 and close April 20 (2025 cycle); council awards in May (marketing) and June/July (facade). 2026 cycle dates not posted as of research date.
annual_pool: Off-Season Tourism Marketing Grant: $30,000 per year (max $3,000 per award; only $9,000 awarded in FY2024-25); Facade Improvement Grant: $200,000 (FY2024-25, max $30,000 per award, $291,733 awarded across 12 recipients including a July 2025 supplemental round)
contact: Nan Devlin, Tillamook Coast Visitors Association (grant administrator), nan@tillamookcoast.com, (503) 355-2291; City of Rockaway Beach (503) 374-1752; City Manager Luke Shepard
notes: The city funds two lodging-tax grant programs administered by the Tillamook Coast Visitors Association: an Off-Season Tourism Marketing Grant ($30,000 pool, up to $3,000, for tourism businesses and nonprofits marketing to visitors from 50+ miles, reimbursement basis) and a Facade Improvement Grant ($200,000, up to $30,000, for-profit tourism businesses only). TCVA screens for eligibility and the City Council approves awards by resolution. The city's grandfathered ordinance lets it spend 51% of TLT on city services; a 2025 ordinance amendment broadened allowed tourism uses beyond media advertising. Separate Small and Large Community Grants (city budget, nonprofits, March and April deadlines) are not TLT-funded.

presentation.pattern: No applicant presentation; TCVA reviews applications for eligibility and completeness and the City Council approves awards at a regular meeting

meeting_schedule: City Council regular meetings second Wednesday of the month; marketing awards approved May 14, 2025 (Res. 2025-27), facade awards by Res. 2025-32 and Res. 2025-42 (July 16, 2025)
pool_note: City TLT about $2.54M per year; 51% may go to city services under the grandfathered ordinance. Dollars open to outside applicants: $30,000 marketing grants plus $200,000 facade grants (FY2024-25 budget), about $230,000; the rest funds the TCVA marketing contract, city facilities and services.

deadline_pattern: City Economic Development Division sets one deadline each year; recent deadlines were Oct 13, 2023, Aug 12, 2024, Aug 12, 2025 and Feb 1, 2026 (the Feb 2026 round may reflect a shift to a winter cycle; next date not posted)
typical_open: About four to six weeks before the deadline (summer for the August rounds; early January for the Feb 2026 round)
annual_pool: 12% of the city's eligible tourism (TLT) funds; individual grants $1,000 to $10,000, with priority projects typically $2,500 to $5,000
contact: City of Grants Pass Economic Development Division (named contact not published in sources reviewed)
notes: The city's Tourism Promotion Grant Program (called the Sustainable Tourism Grant Program in 2023-24) sets aside 12% of eligible TLT for grants of $1,000 to $10,000 to registered businesses or nonprofits inside the city limits or UGB for marketing tied to events and activities that draw visitors from 50+ miles or generate overnight stays. Priority goes to recurring events with growth potential (sports, arts, cultural and food festivals, industry gatherings), outdoor recreation, historic sites and off-peak tourism; a grant review committee ranks complete applications. The bulk of tourism TLT (28% of net) goes to Visit Grants Pass under contract, and the city spends its full 30% unrestricted share on public safety. City pages could not be fetched directly, so pool size and the 2027 date are unconfirmed.
pool_note: City TLT about $1.53M per year. Grant pool is 12% of eligible tourism funds (if the 70% tourism share is about $1.07M, 12% would be roughly $130,000, but the city's own figure was not located); 28% of net TLT goes to Visit Grants Pass; 30% to public safety.

name: Union County
tax_rate: 3% county-wide (Ordinance 2020-01, revised by Ordinance 2025-03 adopted after a May 21, 2025 hearing) + 1.5% state
deadline_pattern: Community Event funding applications are due May 31 for the following fiscal year (Ordinance 2025-03; the 2023 round ran June 1 to July 14); the Transient Tax Advisory Committee recommends and the Board of Commissioners approves in late June. Discretionary grants are reviewed as received while funds last.
typical_open: Spring (applications posted on the county website)
annual_pool: $51,000 event pool in 2026 ($41,730 awarded); $96,894 awarded in 2024 across events and attractions. Ordinance 2025-03 allocates 15% of the 3% tax to events and 10% to discretionary grants.
contact: Union County Administrative Office, 1106 K Avenue, La Grande, OR 97850, 541-963-1001, commissioners@union-county.org (Commissioners Paul Anderes panderes@union-county.org, Matt Scarfo mscarfo@union-county.org, Jake Seavert jseavert@union-county.org)
notes: Union County's 3% transient room tax funds a Community Event and Attraction grant program run by the County Administrative Office: public-sector and nonprofit applicants only, reviewed by a Transient Tax Advisory Committee of up to seven members with final approval by the Board of Commissioners each June. Ordinance 2025-03 fixes the split: 27% tourism promotion, 10% Union County Chamber, 6% small cities, 15% events, 10% discretionary grants, 7% Mt. Emily Recreation Area, 8% Buffalo Peak Golf Course, 8% fairgrounds, 5% sheriff, 3% search and rescue, 1% safe rides. Recent awards favor festivals, advertising budgets, trail work and fairground facilities (Eastern Oregon Film Festival $18,000 in 2026).
members_source: https://unioncountyor.gov/community-event-attraction-funding-available/ ; Transient Tax Advisory Committee member names not published

presentation.pattern: No presentation described; written applications reviewed by the advisory committee

meeting_schedule: Board of Commissioners regular sessions Wednesdays at the Joseph Annex, La Grande; grant approvals at the late-June meeting (June 26, 2024; June 25, 2026)
pool_note: County TRT revenue not published; the 2026 event grant pool was $51,000 (15% events plus 10% discretionary under the 2025 ordinance). 27% goes to tourism promotion and 10% to the chamber under contract.
